newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian held for penning letter bomb claim letters.
newsitem.headline: Austrian held for penning letter bomb claim letters.

text.p: A 62-year-old Austrian computer expert was arrested on Wednesday on suspicion of having penned letters claiming responsibility for a series of letter bombs.
The man, identified only as Gerhard P, was taken into custody after the issuing of an arrest warrant by the Vienna District Court.
The man underwent three hours of questioning during which he insisted on his innocence, a court spokesman said.
He was suspected of having written two claim letters to current affairs magazines Profil and News on December 1, 1996, and February 25, 1997.

Interior Minister Karl Schloegl said he could not rule out that Gerhard P had links to the actual letter bomb attacks but police had not found proof of this. Police have no concrete suspects in the attacks so far.
Since 1993, four people have been killed by either letter or pipe bombs in Austria, with a further 13 injured in the attacks.
The bombs were largely targeted at foreigners living in Austria, people belonging to minority groups or those who support the integration of foreigners.
